claims.text: Local chemical order and dislocation dynamics influence the dynamic mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys.
Interaction between local chemical order and dislocation dynamics enhances both strength and ductility in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed hypothesis applies to as-cast or annealed high-entropy alloys.
Changing alloy composition, thermomechanical processing, or defect content can serve as interventions affecting the proposed behavior.
The relevant dynamic mechanical response depends on strain rate and temperature.
Local chemical order and dislocation dynamics are the structural mediators of the mechanical response.
Interaction between local chemical order and dislocation dynamics produces stable dislocation configurations.
Stable dislocation configurations enhance the strength and ductility of high-entropy alloys.
High-entropy alloys will have greater strength and ductility than traditional alloys of similar composition.
Relative to the baseline, yield strength will increase by 10–20%.
Relative to the baseline, elongation at break will increase by 5–10%.
The hypothesis should hold across high-entropy alloys with a variety of compositions and processing conditions.
The hypothesis may not apply to alloys with very low or very high entropy.
